subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Drivers of overall airline passenger experience/satisfaction, decomposed into service and operational facets

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: A coherent experience facet capturing in-flight crew service tone.

per_column.name: seat_comfort_and_space
per_column.rationale: Physical comfort facet of the experience.

per_column.name: aircraft_condition_recency
per_column.rationale: Aircraft condition facet; but near-duplicate of aircraft_age_and_condition.

per_column.name: operational_disruption
per_column.rationale: Operational reliability facet; but near-duplicate of operational_disruption_and_reliability.

per_column.name: service_consistency_trend
per_column.rationale: Temporal consistency facet; near-duplicate of service_consistency_and_trend.

per_column.name: amenity_availability
per_column.rationale: Service scope facet of the experience.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on one coherent, data-inferable focus: the facets driving overall airline passenger experience/satisfaction (crew, seat, food, aircraft, operations, ground, value, consistency). This is an actionable framing an analyst could investigate to identify which aspect most affects Overall Rating/Recommended. Focus coherence is strong. However, structure quality is weakened by substantial redundancy: roughly five facets are duplicated near-verbatim (aircraft condition, operational disruption, service consistency, ground/check-in, value for money), so the added set is padded with restated columns rather than a clean, differentiated facet decomposition. Several facets (seat, food, value) also merely re-encode existing original numeric ratings as categoricals, adding limited new granularity. The core inferred focus is sound and useful, but the executed structure is inflated and not cleanly parsimonious.
